newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ARA mogas storage slashed as backwardation soars.
newsitem.headline: ARA mogas storage slashed as backwardation soars.

text.p: Stores of gasoline in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp market have reached their lowest levels this year with backwardation at its widest for eight months, storage industry sources said on Thursday. More expensive prompt oil discourages stockpiling.
"The backwardated market means it's almost impossible to store. Stocks are very much lower than, say, two months ago, and a little lower than a month ago," one industry source said.

This week, an estimated 400,000 tonnes of gasoline were in storage in independent companies in ARA. However, the Dutch government's compulsory stock requirement of 277,000 tonnes of gasoline means that the level of usable product is little more than 100,000 tonnes.
Stocks at refineries can provide little extra even though reasonably healthy margins have led refiners to run at full capacity, traders say.
Independent gasoline stocks are supported by the market's core trading companies who have to maintain their storage contracts.
"There are players with year long contracts. You have at least four players each with about 30 to 40 cubes (thousand cubic metres)," one storage source said.
Stocks are not at an all-time low, but some in the industry believe the levels could dip further in the next month with no sign of gasoline's strength easing.
"I have a (gasoline) contract that could be prolonged into August, but it looks like the space may have to be switched to other products," one storage source said.

Traders say the tightness of the prompt market is likely to continue at least until the middle of the August with continuing demand in the United States and little product available in northern Europe or the Mediterranean.
"Demand doesn't seem to be getting any less. Supply is tight in the U.S. and Europe. Where's the gasoline going to come from? Maybe from Saudi Arabia," one trader said.
The backwardation between the front months, August and September, of the gasoline swaps market reached about $9 a tonne this week.
Except for one day at the start of June, such levels have not been seen for eight months.
As recently as July 15, the front month swaps were in contango.
